REFUTED -- doc accuracy on scope: docs/architecture/atlas-plugin-map-2026-07-17.md line 41 explicitly states the debounce uses 'own run-scoped counter at .atlas/.run/docs_drift_watch.json'. This is false: `grep -n session plugins/atlas/hooks/docs_drift_watch.py` returns zero matches -- the state file is keyed only by repo root (_state_path(root) = root/.atlas/.run/docs_drift_watch.json), with no session_id, run id, or any other scoping in the key, the read, or the write. No cleanup/rmtree of .atlas/.run/docs_drift_watch.json was found in scripts/*.py. A brand-new session in the same repo inherits whatever streak count a prior, unrelated session left behind, so the docstring's own claim 'warns on the first drifting edit' is not guaranteed per-session -- it is guaranteed only per-repo, contradicting both the doc line and the implicit per-run framing of the docstring. This is untested: test_docs_drift_watch.py has no test that starts a second logical session against a pre-existing state file. NEEDS-EVIDENCE -- concurrency: _load_state/_save_state is an unlocked, non-atomic read-modify-write (plain path.write_text, no file lock, no tmp+rename). Two concurrent Edit-tool invocations in the same run racing on the same state file can lose an increment (last writer wins) or, in principle, interleave a partial write if killed mid-write_text. No test covers this; not exercised here either (would need a true concurrent-process repro, which this pass did not construct). CONFIRMED cost concern -- measured `python3 docs_drift_watch.py` end-to-end (git rev-parse + 2x git diff as real subprocesses) over 20 sequential edits in a tiny throwaway repo: avg 38.1ms, max 46.2ms per invocation; isolated python3 subprocess-launch overhead alone measured ~17.4ms, so the git calls contribute roughly another ~20ms on top, on every single non-docs Edit/Write/MultiEdit regardless of debounce streak (the debounce only suppresses the printed warning, not the git subprocess calls themselves). Cost was measured on a near-empty repo; not verified against a large repo's git diff cost. PASS -- hook count: hooks.json has 19 total command entries covering 13 distinct scripts (auto_skill, bash_advisor, chronicle_facet, completion_gate, dispatch_tripwire, docs_drift_watch, format_after_edit, ingest_session, memory_capture, nudge, prompt_optimizer, session_boot, atlas_doctor.py --hook); plugins/atlas/README.md's hook table (lines 86-98) lists exactly these same 13 rows with no omissions or extras, chronicle_facet.py included. OVERALL: the self-certified entry's test-count and extraction claims hold up, but it overstates the debounce as 'run-scoped' when the code is repo-global with no session concept at all -- a concrete inaccuracy in docs/architecture/atlas-plugin-map-2026-07-17.md:41 that a reader would take as verified fact. Concurrency safety is also unproven, not merely under-tested. Net verdict is needs-evidence, not verified: the run-scoping claim needs either a code fix (embed session_id in the state key) or a doc correction to 'repo-scoped, not session-scoped', and the concurrency question needs either a lock/atomic-write fix or an explicit note that concurrent Edits are not supported.

claim: Adversarial re-verification of the needs-verification entry for docs_drift_watch.py's three fixes (session scoping, git-cache TTL, atomic state write).
evidence:
PERF (highest priority): 20 sequential real subprocess invocations of docs_drift_watch.py. Throwaway git repo: avg 21.86ms / max 37.98ms (first call/cache-miss 38.0ms, calls 2-20/cache-hits ~20.4-22.0ms) vs bare python3 -c pass baseline avg 14.80ms/max 15.98ms. This repo (tech-tools, larger): avg 22.94ms / max 41.31ms (first call 41.3ms, hits ~20.8-23.6ms). Both confirm the TTL cache materially helps (down from the prior 38.13ms avg baseline) though ~6-7ms of per-call overhead remains above bare python startup (imports + always-on state-file write), which is expected and not a defect.
CACHE CROSS-PROCESS VALIDITY (the likely-bug hypothesis, refuted): wrapped the real git binary with a counting shim on PATH and ran 20 sequential real subprocess invocations against a throwaway repo. Only 3 git invocations total occurred (1x rev-parse + 2x diff, all on call #1); calls 2-20 (19 calls, separate OS processes) made zero git calls -- proving time.monotonic()-keyed cache written by process A is genuinely read and honored by process B on darwin arm64 (Python 3.14.6). Directly confirmed monotonic is comparable cross-process here: 3 sequential bare python3 -c 'print(time.monotonic(), time.time())' calls showed monotonic deltas matching wall-clock deltas to the millisecond (e.g. mono diff 3.023s vs wall diff 3.022s over a 3s sleep). This is because CLOCK_MONOTONIC/mach continuous time on macOS is boot-relative and system-wide, not per-process -- the theoretical objection does not hold on this platform.
SESSION SCOPING E2E (raw subprocess, not unit test): built a streak of 3 under session_id='old' (state file confirmed streak:3), then one edit under session_id='new' warned immediately (stdout contained the docs-drift message), then a second edit under the same 'new' session was silent (stdout '') -- exactly the reset-then-resume contract.

Repo root ships pyrightconfig.json with extraPaths including plugins/atlas/hooks specifically for this; running pyright from any cwd under the repo (hooks dir or repo root, relative or absolute path) gives 0 errors/0 warnings. Two config defects in series: (D1) serena 1.6 made `languages:` a ProjectConfig field with no default (FIELDS_WITHOUT_DEFAULTS), and every .serena/project.yml on this machine predates the rename and carries only `language_servers:`, so serena_config.py:569 `data["languages"]` raises KeyError and the project is skipped at load; (D2) ~/.mcp.json:57 -- the entry the session actually reads, per .claude/settings.local.json enabledMcpjsonServers -- launched the server with `--context claude-code` and no `--project`, so nothing activated even where the yml was valid. The initial determination ("native LSP subsumes serena, remove it") was WRONG and is recorded as a correction: LSP takes (filePath, line, character) and returns locations, find_symbol takes a name and returns a body; serena's symbol-edit tools (replace_symbol_body, rename_symbol, safe_delete_symbol, replace_in_files) have no native equivalent; and serena's claude-code context excludes read_file/create_text_file/execute_shell_command/find_file/list_dir/search_for_pattern by construction, so it never overlapped lean-ctx or context-mode. title: MCP remote-server auth facts behind the atlas-gateway design (Clerk chosen over Entra)
evidence: MCP spec 2025-06-18 authorization: server MUST publish RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, MUST return WWW-Authenticate on 401, MUST validate token audience; DCR is SHOULD (modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization)

Claude Code supports pre-configured OAuth clients (claude mcp add-json with oauth.clientId + --client-secret), --callback-port, oauth.authServerMetadataUrl and oauth.scopes (docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp)
Entra has no RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, so an Entra-fronted MCP server forces a per-operator client id/secret plus fixed callback port

Clerk supports BOTH dynamic client registration and Client ID Metadata Documents, and ships @clerk/mcp-tools 0.6.0 on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (clerk.com/docs/expressjs/guides/ai/mcp/build-mcp-server)
Clerk supports Microsoft Entra as an enterprise connection via SAML and OIDC/EASIE (clerk.com enterprise-connections/overview)

Azure App Service Easy Auth publishes the protected-resource metadata from WEBSITE_AUTH_PRM_DEFAULT_WITH_SCOPES; APIM can front MCP servers but the tenant has no APIM instance (az resource list, subscription 'Henssler Azure')
No off-the-shelf aggregator fits: npm registry search returns mcp-proxy 6.7.11 (single stdio server to SSE) and no gateway doing auth + per-user tool filtering + credential injection
6 of 11 atlas connectors use OAuth2 client credentials and 5 use API keys or HMAC pairs, so no gateway removes per-vendor credential provisioning; it only moves it from every user to one admin
reproduction: Documentation facts; re-verify against the cited URLs before building.
proposed_fix: User decision: Clerk alone as authorization server, Clerk organization custom permissions as the sole grant store, one app permission per connector, plugin keeps its local stdio connectors. Design awaiting approval before any spec is written.
